transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Head of Search, Lantana), Lina Chen (ML Eng), Samir Patel (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Priya our solutions engineer is here to run through a quick hosted API demo for embeddings + reranking and show the Console/Optimize suggestions. How's everyone doing?

[00:12] Marco: Good, thanks. We're eager. We want to see how it'd fit into our marketplace search, key metric is sub-200ms 95th for product title + attrs. Also data residency and PII concerns.

[00:24] Jordan: Totally, will call those out. Priya, can you take it away?

[00:28] Priya (SE): Sure. Quick agenda — 1) API flow for vectorize -> search -> rerank, 2) Console tracing and token/latency breakdown, 3) Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization), 4) Q&A and next steps. I'll share my screen.

[01:02] Priya: First the embedding endpoint — hosted embeddings is a simple POST to /v1/embeddings with your model id. Example payload here, we use a production tuned open-embedding-4b (note: names sometimes differ) that gives stable vectors at 1536 dims. Response includes embedding float array.

[01:25] Lina: Quick question — do you store embeddings on Redwood side or is it stateless? We want to own the vectors in our DB.

[01:31] Priya: Good callout. Hosted embeddings do not persist your application vectors unless you opt into Redwood Vector Index (managed index add-on). By default it's a stateless API so you pull vector and store in your DB. If you use Redwood-managed indexes, we do store with encryption at rest and KMS; retention and export controls available.

[01:55] Marco: Hmm okay, we probably will keep vectors ourselves. PII: product descriptions might include seller PII. Need audit logs and SSO for access.

[02:06] Jordan: Redwood has audit logs, RBAC, and SAML SSO integrations — we'll share the security pack. Priya will show Console where audit events are surfaced.

[02:18] Priya: Switching to the reranker flow — typical pattern: initial retrieval using your vector DB (we demo FAISS in the playground) -> call Redwood reranker endpoint with top-K candidates + the original query. The reranker scores and returns reordered items with explanations (if enabled). Example API: POST /v1/rerank with {query, candidates:[{id, text, embedding?} ]}.

[02:50] Marco: Is the reranker using cross-encoders? How heavy is it?

[02:55] Priya: Yes, it's a cross-encoder style reranker that runs the candidate list together which is higher compute per request but gives much better precision. For hosted we've got optimized variants and can fall back to cheaper bi-encoder scoring if low latency/cost is critical. We can also do truncated contexts and cached candidate embeddings to reduce cost.

[03:18] Samir: So for 200ms 95p, is cross-encoder realistic?

[03:22] Priya: It depends on K and sequence length. For K=5 and short product titles, our optimized cross-encoder on GPU can hit ~120-160ms p95 in our benchmarks. If you need <100ms p95, you'd either reduce K, use a quantized model host, or do hybrid approach: cheap initial score for p50/p90 then a cross-encoder fallback for ambiguous queries. We'll include the specific benchmark spreadsheet.

[03:50] Jordan: Also note Redwood Dedicated offers reserved capacity for lower jitter vs shared hosted. But since you're starting POC we'd demo hosted and show where Dedicated would fit later.

[04:05] Marco: Sounds good. Show us the Console traces.

[04:09] Priya: On screen — Redwood Console. Here you can see per-route latency percentiles, token counts, and cost breakdown per request. This trace is an embedding->search->rerank walk: embedding call took 48ms, DB lookup 10ms (simulated), rerank took 132ms, total 205ms. We surface where time is spent, so you can decide to tune model or batching.

[04:46] Lina: I see a "prefix cache" metric — what is that?

[04:50] Priya: Prefix/KV cache is our cached past key-value states for chat or repeated prefixes; for rerank we use cached candidate embeddings to avoid recomputing. In Console you can turn on automatic prefix caching and see hit rates. That reduces both latency and cost for repeated queries.

[05:05] Marco: If we store vectors ourselves, can Redwood cache candidate vectors on request path?

[05:10] Priya: Yes — we can cache ephemeral copies of vectors for a TTL on the serving layer, doesn't change your ownership; it's an on-path cache and honors TTLs and evictions.

[05:22] Samir: Security — how are customer keys handled? KMS?

[05:26] Jordan: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for hosted we use our KMS but provide key wrap options. We can provide SOC2/ISO docs and have audit logging showing KMS ops. I'll drop the security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (note: placeholder).

[05:46] Priya: Back to Optimize: this is an engine that suggests model+quantization+batching settings based on your workload. In this demo I ran Optimize on a sample logs set and it suggested: quantize reranker to 8-bit int for batch sizes >8, set per-route max tokens to 128, and use continuous batching window of 12ms to improve throughput without harming p95.

[06:20] Marco: Can we see the suggested CP (cost per thousand requests) delta?

[06:24] Priya: Yep — Optimize shows estimated token cost delta as well as latency impact. For our sample it suggested a 38% cost reduction with a 12% p95 increase; you can tune the knob more conservatively. We'll share the exact numbers.

[06:38] Lina: For the rerank endpoint do you allow returning intermediate scores and top-k explanations for debugging?

[06:44] Priya: Yes, with the debug flag you get score breakdown and attention-lite explanations; note debug increases tokens. Console will also persist recent rerank traces for 7/30/90 days depending on retention plan.

[07:00] Jordan: Quick demo of the API call sequence — I'll paste a sample cURL in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-embeddings (demo link) and rerank doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/rerank-api. Example shows batching multiple queries in a single embeddings call, then upsert to vector DB, then a rerank POST sending candidate ids.

[07:28] Speaker 1 (auto-gen): [inaudible]...

[07:33] Priya: One pattern we recommend: do an offline quantization pass for your reranker model (we recommend 4/8-bit depending on accuracy) and then use Redwood Optimize which will automatically pick the model bundle for the hosted runtime. This avoids you manually swapping models mid-pilot.

[07:58] Marco: What's the onboarding timeline for a POC? We want to run experiments in prod slice for 2 weeks.

[08:05] Jordan: Typical POC is 2–4 weeks: week 0 setup + data ingest, week 1 tuning and baseline, week 2 A/B tests and performance sweep. If you provide sample data fast we can compress it.

[08:16] Lina: We currently use Postgres + an off-the-shelf FAISS service. Our infra team is small; minimal ops is preferred. How much work to integrate?

[08:27] Priya: For stateless embeddings + your own FAISS, it's just API calls from your ingestion pipeline. We have SDKs in Python/Node. If you want Redwood managed index, we can onboard with a small connector and handle sharding. Integration usually takes a couple days for a basic sync.

[08:45] Samir: Cost — do you have transparent cost per token + per-rerank-call?

[08:50] Jordan: Yes, hosted pricing shows per-embedding token cost + per-rerank call (model compute). We'll include a sample cost model in the pricing doc. For heavy rerank usage, Dedicated makes economics more predictable.

[09:02] Marco: Any customers in marketplace vertical?

[09:06] Jordan: We have a few commerce customers — won't name ops here but we'll match reference. I'll connect you with a peer in a similar setup if you'd like.

[09:15] Lina: Ok can we do a short technical deep-dive now on latency tuning?

[09:19] Priya: Sure. We covered model variant, quantization, batching, caching, and routing (regional). A deeper trick: smart routing — send cold queries to lower-cost region while hot traffic routed to a low-latency region. Also our runtime can do continuous batching with latency SLAs — set a max wait time and we aggregate tiny requests to better GPU utilization.

[09:46] Marco: Continuous batching sounds risky for p95. How do you trade-off?

[09:50] Priya: You set SLOs per route; the runtime will never exceed your configured p95 target. Optimize suggests safe batching windows based on historical latency distribution. The Console simulates impact before you apply.

[10:05] Samir: For model explainability — how much access to internal attention etc? Our compliance team may ask for traceability of why a result surfaced.

[10:16] Priya: We provide score breakdowns and optional attention-lite explanations. For regulated audits we can provide deterministic logs of rerank inputs and outputs. For deeper model internals you'd need Private deployment where you can run custom explainability tools on-prem.

[10:35] Marco: If we want to keep vectors in-house but use Redwood hosted reranker, any data flow concerns?

[10:41] Priya: You'd send candidate texts or ids with embeddings attached in the rerank call. If embeddings are sensitive you can send ephemeral hashes or serve them via signed URLs — we support a few patterns. We'll document the patterns for your security team.

[10:59] Lena? (auto): Sorry, misread.

[11:05] Jordan: I'll flag compliance folks to join later. On the POC side we usually run a traffic mirror for a small percent so no customer-facing risk.

[11:13] Priya: Demo time — I'll run a live rerank with our demo dataset. Starting query: "waterproof hiking boots men's size 10". Initial vector retrieval returns 20 candidates, we pass top-8 to the reranker. Reranker returns reordered list with scores: candidate 237 (0.91), 153 (0.87), 402 (0.84).

[11:45] Lina: That reordering looks better than baseline, I like the title normalization. How are synonyms handled?

[11:51] Priya: The reranker leverages contextual embeddings plus title/descr cross-encoder; synonyms are handled implicitly. You can also pass seller metadata as additional context fields.

[12:08] Marco: Can we tune to prefer our preferred sellers or sponsored items?

[12:12] Priya: Yes — reranker accepts a biasing signal or a post-score multiplier. We recommend keeping business rules outside the model for auditable policies: apply a final business-weighted reorder step after rerank scores.

[12:30] Samir: About metrics — do you provide precision@k, MRR, NDCG in Console?

[12:36] Priya: We have a metrics dashboard in Console; for custom metrics like MRR you'll upload labelled testset and Console can compute NDCG, precision@k per variant. We'll import your query labels for A/B.

[12:52] Marco: We'll need per-route SLA and billing alerts.

[12:55] Jordan: Alerts are supported — set thresholds for cost, latency, and token usage with Slack/email hooks.

[13:05] Priya: One more thing: cold-start for new SKUs — we recommend a multi-stage strategy: (1) use title-only embeddings initially, (2) run cheap bi-encoder for freshness, (3) trigger cross-encoder for queries with low confidence. Optimize helps pick thresholds.

[13:27] Lina: For data privacy — retention windows for traces and console logs?

[13:31] Priya: Default 30 days, can be configured to 7/30/90/365 on enterprise plans. Audit logs are configurable and downloadable for audits.

[13:45] Samir: Let's talk pricing now briefly.

[13:48] Jordan: I'll send the formal pricing doc but high level: embeddings per 1k tokens, rerank per call (tiered by model), and optional managed index + storage. There's volume discounts and Dedicated reserved capacity pricing for heavy consistent workloads.

[14:05] Marco: We have an internal procurement window late May — any blockers for a 2-week POC in April?

[14:12] Jordan: No blockers on our side. We can do a self-serve onboarding and pilot under a trial account. We'll provide a checklist for your infra and legal teams.

[14:22] Priya: I'll now show the Optimize UI — it has a slider for cost vs latency preference, and it will generate recommended model/quantization/batch settings. You can preview the expected p95 impact and cost delta. Here's a sample run I did on a Lantana-like workload in the sandbox.

[14:46] Lina: Can Optimize run automatically on live traffic?

[14:50] Priya: It can run scheduled sweeps and suggest changes; we don't auto-apply without explicit approval. You can enable auto-rollouts in Dedicated with safeguards.

[14:59] Marco: Are there SDKs for quick integration, examples in Node for express?

[15:04] Jordan: Yes Python, Node, Java. We'll share quickstart templates and a Postman collection. Link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart (placeholder).

[15:15] Priya: Wrapping up the technical bits — tradeoffs and recommended starting config for your pilot: hosted embeddings stateless, managed FAISS or your own, rerank K=8 with cross-encoder quantized to 8-bit, continuous batch window 12ms, caching TTL 30s for hot candidates. This should give your target p95 around 160-210ms in test.

[15:45] Marco: That looks reasonable. We'll confirm the sample data for Lina to upload.

[15:52] Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan send pricing + SOW, Priya share benchmark CSV + console export, Lina upload sample docs/queries. We'll schedule POC start once data is in. Any other Qs?

[16:05] Samir: One small ask — can your security team provide a short note on data flow for vectors? We'll need to present to compliance.

[16:11] Jordan: Yes, security pack + a one-page data flow diagram — will attach.

[16:17] Marco: Great, thanks.

[16:20] Priya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links.

[16:24] Speaker 2 (auto-gen): [unintelligible crosstalk]...

[16:30] Jordan: Bye all.

[16:32] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: Automated speaker detection sometimes labeled participants generically, a few words mis-transcribed (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), and some timestamps approximate. Links shared in chat are placeholders for internal docs.
